title: Integrated Cashflow Scenario Playbook for Commitments and Billing
author: Maya Chen
content:
Purpose and scope

This playbook explains how Finance, Legal, Procurement and Sales coordinate to produce consistent cashflow forecasts, billing schedules, and revenue recognition outcomes for contracts that include committed or reserved capacity ("Dedicated" offers). It consolidates common scenarios, decision triggers, required metadata, and example journal entries. Use this document when closing or amending capacity commitments, planning forecast scenarios, or preparing monthly close adjustments.

Key objectives
- Ensure forecasts match contractual billing triggers and the timing of service performance.
- Standardize handoffs between Sales / Solutions / Procurement and Finance.
- Reduce last-minute forecast corrections at month-end by defining inputs, owners and SLAs.
- Provide reproducible templates for scenario-driven cashflow analysis.

Audience
- Finance (FP&A, RevRec, Accounting)
- Legal and Contracts team
- Sales and Solutions Engineering
- Procurement and Billing Operations
- Customer Success (for acceptance and onboarding timing)

Definitions and required contract metadata
- Committed Monthly Fee: fixed monthly charge for reserved capacity (USD).
- Minimum Contract Term: length in months.
- Start of Service (SoS): date when customer can begin production on provisioned capacity.
- Acceptance Date: date when customer confirmatory acceptance or automatic acceptance criteria are met.
- Billing Trigger: event that causes an invoice (e.g., SoS, contract effective date, first usage).
- Non-Refundable Setup: portion of fee invoiced/recognised upfront.

Every contract record in the CRM (and downstream contract database) must include these fields: contract_id, customer_tier, committed_monthly_fee, minimum_term_months, setup_fee_usd, billing_trigger, start_of_service_date, acceptance_criteria, cancellation_terms, payment_terms_days.

Ownership and SLAs
- Sales: populate contract metadata and tag deal as DEDICATED in CRM at contract signature (SLA 24 hours).
- Legal: verify contract metadata and mark exceptions if billing deviates from standard templates (SLA 48 hours).
- Procurement/Billing Ops: convert contract into subscription record and schedule first invoice (SLA 3 business days after SoS or billing trigger).
- RevRec: verify recognition method and provide forecast impact to FP&A (SLA 2 business days after invoice is scheduled).
- FP&A: update cashflow forecast and scenario models (SLA weekly cadence, and special ad hoc within 2 business days of material contract changes).

Scenario matrix (summary)
|| Scenario || Forecast impact || RevRec trigger || Billing cadence || Primary owner ||
| New Dedicated Contract (standard) | +Committed monthly revenue starts on SoS; one-time setup cash inflow on setup_fee | Revenue ratably over contract unless setup_fee non-refundable (see contract) | Monthly in advance or upfront per contract | Sales -> Billing Ops |
| Contract Amendment (term/fee change) | Delta applied pro‑rata from amendment effective date | RevRec adjusts prospectively; catch-up adjustments if prior invoices were incorrect | Adjusted monthly invoices or credit/memo | Sales + RevRec |
| Early Termination (customer pays termination fee) | Immediate cash inflow (termination fee) and loss of future committed revenue | Termination fee recognized on receipt if not performance-based; remaining prepayments reviewed for refund liability | One-time invoice | Legal + Finance |
| Conversion from Trial / POC to Committed | Forecast steps up over provisioning timeline | Recognize when acceptance and billing trigger met; if trial fees credited, apply credit mechanics | Typically monthly forward billing | Sales + Customer Success |

Detailed procedures and checklists
1) New Dedicated Contract — from signature to first recognized revenue
   a) At signature (Sales): tag CRM record with committed_monthly_fee, minimum_term_months, setup_fee_usd, billing_trigger and expected SoS.
   b) Legal: confirm billing_trigger language ("upon provisioning", "upon acceptance", or "on effective date"). If nonstandard, create a Contract Exception and notify RevRec.
   c) Solutions/Infra: open onboarding ticket (JIRA/Runbook) to provision capacity. Provisioning ETA must be captured in CRM within 24 hours.
   d) Customer Success: capture acceptance criteria and plan acceptance call; set tentative acceptance date.
   e) Billing Ops: schedule first invoice based on billing_trigger. If billing_trigger = SoS and provisioning is ahead of schedule, Billing Ops waits for documented Acceptance Date.
   f) RevRec: determine recognition policy: typically ratable over the minimum_term_months starting on SoS or Acceptance Date. For any non-refundable setup_fee, tag as "setup_revenue" and recognize per contract terms (either upfront or amortized).
   g) FP&A: insert contract cashflows to short-term forecast using scheduled invoice dates and payment terms (use expected collection delay of payment_terms_days plus processing lag of 3 business days).

2) Amendment workflow — mid‑contract fee or term change
   a) Sales must create an amendment record and mark the amendment_effective_date.
   b) RevRec computes prospective revenue delta and any catch-up adjustments for previously billed periods (generate journal entries for credits/debits).
   c) Billing Ops issues credit or debit memos for historical corrections; confirm customer acceptance of any credits.
   d) FP&A updates scenario models and publishes an updated cashflow delta to Treasury.

3) Early termination and settlement
   a) Legal validates termination fee per contract.
   b) Billing Ops issues settlement invoice.
   c) RevRec assesses whether remaining prepayments are refundable or should be recognized as termination income.
   d) FP&A models future cash shortfall and flags to leadership if >5% of quarterly forecast; scenario to be published within 24 hours.

Forecast templates and modeling inputs
- Minimum input columns (CSV): contract_id, customer_name, product_line, committed_monthly_fee_usd, setup_fee_usd, minimum_term_months, start_of_service_date, acceptance_date, billing_trigger, payment_terms_days, currency, region, sales_owner, contract_owner.
- Suggested FP&A model tabs: ActiveContracts, Amendments, Terminations, CollectionsLag, FX assumptions, DeferredRevenueSchedule.

Sample calculations
- Monthly recognized revenue (ratable basis):
  recognized_monthly = committed_monthly_fee_usd * proportion_of_service_days_in_month
  Example: committed_monthly_fee = 120,000 USD/year => 10,000 USD/month. If SoS is on the 11th of a 30-day month: proportion = (30 - 10)/30 = 20/30 => first month recognized = 6,667 USD.
- Deferred revenue on setup_fee if amortized over term:
  deferred_setup_monthly = setup_fee_usd / minimum_term_months

Example journal entries (illustrative)
- On invoice issuance (monthly in advance):
  DR Accounts Receivable 10,000
  CR Unearned Revenue (Deferred Revenue) 10,000

- On monthly recognition (ratable):
  DR Unearned Revenue 10,000
  CR Service Revenue 10,000

- On setup_fee received and recognized upfront (non-refundable):
  DR Cash 25,000
  CR Service Revenue 25,000

Note: These entry examples are illustrative. RevRec and Accounting must validate against GAAP/IFRS and consult external or internal accounting counsel for complex arrangements.

Controls and review checklist for monthly close
- Verify all dedicated contracts with SoS within the month are present in RevRec tracker (owner: RevRec).
- Reconcile invoices scheduled vs. invoices issued (owner: Billing Ops). Threshold: 100% of scheduled invoices must be issued or have a documented exception.
- Cash collection lag: Flag any invoice unpaid after payment_terms_days + 10 days as delinquent; escalate to AR collector.
- FX remeasurement: apply monthly FX spot to AR balances by region and post P&L impact (owner: Accounting).

Procurement / Purchase Order alignment (when applicable)
- If enterprise customers require PO-based invoicing: Sales must capture PO number and PO billing cadence. Billing Ops must verify PO acceptance before scheduling the first invoice.
- For capitalized or pass-through procurement charges (hardware, installation partners): Procurement must map vendor invoices to contract_id and tag as reimbursable if contract specifies.

Exception handling and contract deviations
- Contracts that deviate from the standard (custom billing cadence, multi-year prepaid with unique refund mechanics) must be escalated to RevRec and Legal and marked with label CONTRACT_EXCEPTION in CRM.
- Exception SLAs: initial assessment within 48 hours; treatment (revrec policy) published within 5 business days.

Reporting and dashboards
- Weekly FP&A feed: new committed ARR, churned committed ARR, expected cash in next 30/60/90 days.
- Monthly close package: deferred revenue rollforward, contract amendment summary, and top 10 forecast deltas with root-cause.
- Alerts: Treasury receives an automated alert when expected cash inflows > $250k shift vs prior forecast (owner: FP&A).

Appendices
A. Quick checklist for Sales at signature
- Populate all required CRM fields (see section above).
- Attach signed contract PDF and mark "DEDICATED" tag.
- Notify Solutions for provisioning with expected SoS.

B. CSV import template (column header row)
- contract_id,customer_name,product_line,committed_monthly_fee_usd,setup_fee_usd,minimum_term_months,start_of_service_date,acceptance_date,billing_trigger,payment_terms_days,currency,region,sales_owner,contract_owner
